# Expense disclosure vs Schedule C — coverage and the appendix question

**Generated by:** `code/reconcile_disclosure_schedule_c.py` (stdlib, no network) from committed files only: `data/fyNN/expense_disclosure/` (the Council's disclosure workbooks, retrieved 2026-07-15) and `data/fyNN/schedule_c/` + `data/recovered/`. Re-running it on the same files reproduces this report byte for byte; `code/test_reconcile_disclosure_schedule_c.py` fails if it is stale.

**Key:** `(EIN, amount)` within one fiscal year, matched as a multiset. Never EIN alone, never the council member. **Published set** = the Schedule C body + the three appendix CSVs (what the MCP indexes). `data/recovered/schedule_c_appendix_recovered.csv` was built *from* the disclosure, so it is reported separately as **circular** and is never counted as coverage.

**Every figure here is this script's arithmetic on those files. None is a figure the Council publishes.**

## 4. GitHub #57 blocker 2 — are the appendix CSVs additive to the body, or a subset?

Settled per year from the disclosure's own `source` column. **body rows that can only be appendix designations** = body rows whose `(EIN, amount)` the disclosure carries *only* under Local/Aging/Youth. **double-listed** = rows on keys present in both body and appendix beyond what the disclosure itself holds — the same designation printed twice. If the appendices were re-sorted subsets of the body, both would be close to the appendix row count.

The direct test is the column **appendix rows matched after the body**: body rows are matched to the disclosure first, so an appendix row can only match a designation the body did not already claim. A subset would leave that column near zero.

| FY | body rows | appendix rows | appendix rows matched after the body | appendix $ | disclosure L/A/Y rows | disclosure L/A/Y $ (all) | (cleared) | body rows that can only be appendix | $ | double-listed | appendix rows the disclosure files only under an initiative | verdict |

**Reading the verdict.** `NO APPENDIX ROWS`: the year's appendix CSVs are empty (header only; the PDF parse missed them, GitHub #59), so there is nothing to add or to double-count; the disclosure-built sidecar holds that year's appendix awards and was built skipping any `(EIN, amount)` already in the body. `ADDITIVE`: no body row is an appendix-only designation and nothing is double-listed. `ADDITIVE (with exceptions)`: the same, except for the rows listed below — a handful per year against thousands of appendix rows, each a candidate extraction or filing error, not evidence that the appendices repeat the body.
